history.dynasty: Namgyal dynasty (Sikkimese monarchy); renovated to grand proportions by Jigme Pawo, the third re-embodiment of Lhatsun Chempo
history.period: Late 17th century - founded 1697 by Lama Lhatsun Chempo (Gyalwa Lhatsum Chempo); regarded as the second-oldest monastery in Sikkim
history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Geyzing' is approximate - the monastery stands on a ridge above Pelling in Gyalshing district (Geyzing/Gyalshing is the district headquarters town). Known as the 'place of secret spells' ('Sanga Choeling' = Island of the Guhyamantra/secret-mantra teachings). Built in 1697 by Gyalwa Lhatsun Chempo and regarded as the second-oldest monastery in Sikkim, sacred to followers of the Nyingma (Nyingmapa) sect of Tibetan Buddhism; sources say the monastery is reserved for men only. The original structure was damaged by fire several times and rebuilt/remodelled; it houses 17th-century clay statues, wall paintings, scriptures and valuable artifacts. It stands about 7 km from Pemayangtse Monastery and is reached on foot via a steep 4 km forest track (about 40-60 minutes from Pelling). It is part of the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit of Pemayangtse, Rabdentse ruins, Khecheopalri Lake, Norbugang Chorten, Dubdi and Tashiding. COORDINATES FLAG (verify): map.geocode has no POI record for the Pelling monastery (it matched only a namesake in Darjeeling, West Bengal); coordinates 27.26389, 88.22139 are from Wikipedia/GeoHack and agree with trek.zone - but note Wikipedia's current infobox shows Dubdi's founder and 1701 date (an apparent data error), so treat the page's infobox fields with care. Religious affiliation verified as Nyingma Tibetan Buddhism - NOT a Hindu temple.

name: Sanga Choeling Monastery
town_description: Pelling, at about 2,150 m in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim, is Sikkim's premier hill resort town with close views of Kanchenjunga. It lies about 130-145 km west of Gangtok (verify). Nearby attractions include Pemayangtse Monastery, Sanga Choeling Monastery, the Pelling Sky Walk with the Chenrezig statue, Khecheopalri Lake and Darap village.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 145 km (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 145 km (verify).
travel.road: Reached on foot only via a steep 2-4 km forest track from Upper Pelling (a road was reported under construction - verify current status); taxi/shared jeep to Pelling from Gyalshing (Geyzing).

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; winter for snow views, summer for clearer mountain views.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One source reports 9 AM-5 PM (verify); visits are normally during daylight hours.
